description: We are Mechanicats and we are a hybrid team formed by bringing together three pairs.
summary: ACHACHAY data takes on the challenge of adapting agriculture to climate conditions through a digital platform that integrates NASA satellite and meteorological data to identify and monitor frost risk. It turns this data into easy-to-understand maps, indicators, alerts and recommendations, applied to planting and crop rotation planning. Its importance lies in helping Ecuadorian farmers anticipate adverse weather conditions, take preventive action, reduce crop losses, and strengthen the resilience of agricultural production against a changing climate.
details:
What does the project do and how does it work?
The platform lets users look up information based on their location and has three main modules. The first offers frost monitoring for the next three days, temperature maps, environmental indicators, soil moisture, frost history and alerts. The second gives planting suggestions by month and crop, information on crop rotation, and an assistant chatbot. The third presents projections of possible risk scenarios for the coming months, aimed at agricultural planning.

What are its benefits?
ACHACHAY data makes meteorological and satellite information accessible, information that normally takes technical knowledge to interpret. It also brings different environmental variables together in a single platform, lets users explore geographic information, and offers recommendations that can help farmers plan their activities and take preventive measures against adverse weather conditions.

What is the expected impact?
We aim to help reduce agricultural losses caused by frost, strengthen farmers’ ability to adapt to climate variability, and promote agriculture grounded in scientific information. Our goal is to bring technology closer to farming communities, especially small and medium-scale producers in Ecuador’s highlands (the Sierra).

What tools did we use?
We use NASA POWER data for meteorological variables and NASA SMAP data for surface and root-zone soil moisture. To build the platform we used web technologies such as HTML, CSS and JavaScript, along with data visualization tools to present the information through charts, maps and indicators.

What makes the project creative and innovative?
Its main contribution is integrating satellite information, weather monitoring and agricultural guidance into a single platform, turning complex scientific data into practical tools for farmers. We also prioritized an intuitive interface that requires no sign-up, so that people with different levels of experience with technology can use it easily.

What factors did the team consider?
We considered the climatic and geographic conditions of Ecuador’s farming areas, especially differences in altitude, temperature variation, soil moisture and how vulnerable crops are to frost. We also took into account farmers’ needs, how accessible the information is, spatial resolution, and the limitations of satellite data sources. Our aim is to present the data as a reference for decision-making, not as exact measurements for each individual plot.
